name: get_top_movers
description:
Get the top N gaining or losing NSE stocks on a specific date.
Returns stocks sorted by % change with OHLCV details.
If the exact date is a holiday/weekend, returns the nearest trading day.

IMPORTANT — UNADJUSTED PRICES + CORPORATE ACTION CHECK:
% change is computed from raw unadjusted prevClose vs close. A stock with a split or bonus ex-date on the requested date will appear as a top loser with a large negative % (e.g., −50% for 1:1 bonus) even though no actual loss occurred. When presenting top losers: for any stock showing a drop > 20%, call get_corporate_actions(symbol, date, date) to check if the NSE CA data lists an ex-date matching that day. If matched, inform the user: e.g. "BRIGADE shows −50% on 2019-07-26 — confirmed CA: Bonus 1:1 ex-date (NSE data). Not a real market loss." Only flag as CA if confirmed by actual NSE data.

Disclaimer: Information/Data made available through the NSEIL MCP server is for informational and educational purposes only and does not constitute investment advice or recommendation. NSEIL is not responsible for any AI generated Output or predictions

direction.description: Direction: 'gain' for top gainers, 'loss' for top losers.

name: nse_lookup_symbol
description:
Look up NSE ticker symbols by partial name or keyword. Returns matching ticker list only — no price data.
Use this to find the exact NSE symbol before calling other tools.
Faster and lighter than search_symbols when you only need the ticker.

Examples:
  query=HDFC   → [HDFC, HDFCBANK, HDFCLIFE, HDFCAMC, ...]
  query=TATA   → [TATA, TATASTEEL, TATAMOTORS, TATACOMM, ...]
  query=BANK   → [BANKBARODA, BANKINDIA, CANBK, ...]

query.description: Partial symbol or keyword to search. Case-insensitive. Examples: 'HDFC', 'TATA', 'RELIANCE'

name: get_market_mood
description:
Get a factual read of NSE market mood for a day: India VIX level, its change over 1 day / 1 week / 1 month and where it sits in its recent range; how many equity indices rose vs fell; how many mainboard stocks advanced vs declined (when available); and the day's change in the main benchmarks.
The 'reading' fields (broad advance / mixed / broad decline) and VIX 'direction' (rising / falling / flat) follow the fixed rules given in 'method'. They describe the day; they are not a forecast or a buy/sell signal — present them that way.
A section is omitted when its data is not available for the date; do not fill it in.
If the date is a holiday/weekend, the nearest earlier trading day is used — always quote the 'date' field; if a 'warning' is present, tell the user.

name: get_index_valuation
description:
Get the valuation ratios of an NSE equity index — P/E, P/B and dividend yield as published by NSE — and where today's value sits within its own recent range: min, max (with dates), median, mean and percentile.
percentile = share of trading days in the window on which the ratio was lower than the current value (e.g. P/E percentile 90 means P/E was lower on 90% of days).
The window is the look-back requested, limited to the data available: always state window_from / window_to when quoting a percentile, and do not describe it as a long-term or historical average.
Not available for India VIX, bond, USD, leverage or inverse indices.
Always quote the 'date' field as the as-of date; if a 'warning' is present, tell the user.

name: get_corporate_actions
description:
Fetch actual NSE corporate action events for a stock directly from NSE India.
Returns splits, bonus issues, dividends, and other events with exact ex-dates.
Only events with an ex-date inside the requested from/to range are returned. If the response has an 'error', the lookup failed — do not treat that as "no corporate actions". If it has a 'warning', the list is incomplete.
ALWAYS call this before get_stock_history or get_price_performance when the user asks about historical prices, returns, or performance for any symbol. Use the returned exDate values to cross-check price discontinuities in the history. The adjustmentFactor field tells you how to interpret pre-event prices:   1:1 bonus → adjustmentFactor=0.5 (pre-bonus prices are 2× the post-bonus equivalent)   10→2 split → adjustmentFactor=0.2 (pre-split prices are 5× the post-split equivalent)
Returns: list of CA events with exDate, purpose (raw NSE text), actionType (SPLIT/BONUS/DIVIDEND/OTHER), adjustmentFactor.
SEBI Disclaimer: This information is for educational and research purposes only. It does not constitute investment advice. Please consult a SEBI-registered investment advisor before making any investment decisions.

name: compare_indices
description:
Compare 2 to 10 NSE indices side by side over the same period: return, annualised volatility, maximum drawdown and current valuation (P/E, P/B, dividend yield). Ranked best to worst by return. Example: Nifty 50 vs Nifty Midcap 100 vs NIFTY Smallcap 100.
Every index is measured between the same base_date and date, both returned. An index with no value on either date is not ranked — it is listed under not_compared with the reason; say so rather than estimating it.
Returns are price-only (dividends excluded) and not annualised. Valuation fields are absent for indices NSE publishes no ratios for.
Always quote 'date' and 'base_date'; if a 'warning' is present, tell the user.

Past performance is not indicative of future results. Please consult a SEBI-registered investment advisor before making any investment decisions.

name: get_stock_history
description:
Get daily OHLCV (Open, High, Low, Close, Volume) price history for an NSE stock.
Returns up to 3 months per call to keep response size manageable.
For longer periods, chain calls using next_end_date from each response.

Example — fetch 1 year of RELIANCE:
  Call 1: symbol=RELIANCE, months=3  (end_date omitted → uses today)
  Call 2: symbol=RELIANCE, months=3, end_date={next_end_date from call 1}
  Call 3: symbol=RELIANCE, months=3, end_date={next_end_date from call 2}
  Call 4: symbol=RELIANCE, months=3, end_date={next_end_date from call 3}

For 2 years: repeat 8 times. Each call returns next_end_date for the next chunk.
If symbol not found, use search_symbols to find the correct symbol.

IMPORTANT — UNADJUSTED PRICES:
All prices are raw NSE bhavcopy data with NO corporate action adjustment.
Before presenting history results, call get_corporate_actions(symbol) to get actual NSE-sourced CA events. Cross-check returned ex-dates with any single-day drop > 20% in the price series. If matched, inform the user: e.g. "Note: INFY shows a -50% drop on 2018-06-14 which is the 1:1 bonus issue ex-date (NSE data) — prices before that date are unadjusted. Adjustment factor: 0.5."

Disclaimer: Information/Data made available through the NSEIL MCP server is for informational and educational purposes only and does not constitute investment advice or recommendation. NSEIL is not responsible for any AI generated Output or predictions.

name: get_stock_vs_index
description:
Compare one NSE stock against a benchmark index over a period: return of each, outperformance in percentage points, beta and correlation.
The stock's return is already adjusted for splits and bonus issues using NSE corporate-action data — do not adjust it again. Events applied are listed under corporate_actions_applied. If that data cannot be obtained, or does not match the price move, the tool returns an error and no figures: report the error, do not substitute numbers from other tools.
If 'warnings' or 'other_corporate_actions' are present (e.g. a demerger or rights issue, which is NOT adjusted for), state them alongside the figures.
Both returns are price-only between the same base_date and date; dividends excluded. Beta and correlation use daily changes and need at least 30 common trading days.
Always quote 'date' and 'base_date'; if a 'warning' is present, tell the user.
SEBI Disclaimer: This information is for educational and research purposes only. It does not constitute investment advice or a recommendation to buy, sell, or hold any securities. Past performance is not indicative of future results. Please consult a SEBI-registered investment advisor before making any investment decisions.

name: compare_stocks
description:

name: get_52_week_high_low
description:
Get the 52-week high and low prices for an NSE stock.
Returns: 52w high/low with dates, current price position within range, % distance from each extreme.

IMPORTANT — UNADJUSTED PRICES + CORPORATE ACTION CHECK:
High/low values are from raw unadjusted bhavcopy data. A split or bonus ex-date within the 52-week window causes an artificial low (the post-event price is a fraction of the pre-event price), which distorts the true 52-week range. Before presenting results: call get_corporate_actions(symbol) (covers last 5 years). Check if any CA ex-date falls within the past 52 weeks (today − 365 days). If yes, flag: e.g. "52W low for INFY may be distorted — 1:1 bonus ex-date 2024-06-14 falls in range (NSE data). The post-bonus price level is not comparable to pre-bonus prices."

name: get_index_performance
description:
Get the price performance of one NSE index: 1-day change plus returns over 1 week, 1 month, 3 months, 6 months, 1 year and 2 years, and the 52-week high/low with dates and distance from each.
Each period return is the close-to-close price change against the last trading day on or before the period start; the response gives that base_date and base_close so the figure can be checked. Returns are not annualised and exclude dividends.
Periods the index has no data for are listed under unavailable_periods — do not estimate them. If high_low_52w.complete_52_weeks is false, the high/low cover only the shorter window shown.
Always quote the 'date' field as the as-of date; if a 'warning' is present, tell the user.
